32080-punch-or-the-london-charivari-vol-.title: Punch Or The London Charivari Vol 158 June 16 1920
32080-punch-or-the-london-charivari-vol-.creator: Unknown
32080-punch-or-the-london-charivari-vol-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. As the result of some remarks let drop by the crew and repeated by the ship's parrot, several hundred bottles of liquor were found on board the _S.S. Curaçao_ by the San Francisco port authorities. It is now suggested, in the interests of philology, that the parrot should be put back to hear how the crew takes it.

arxiv-2105-08075.title: Low temperature photo-physics of single NV centers in diamond
arxiv-2105-08075.creator: Jodok Happacher, David Broadway, Patrick Reiser, Alejandro Jiménez, Märta A. Tschudin, Lucas Thiel, Dominik Rohner, Marcel.li Grimau Puigibert, Brendan Shields, Jeronimo R. Maze, Vincent Jacques, Patrick Maletinsky
arxiv-2105-08075.description: Abstract We investigate the magnetic field dependent photo-physics of individual Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) color centers in diamond under cryogenic conditions. At distinct magnetic fields, we observe significant reductions in the NV photoluminescence rate, which indicate a marked decrease in the optical readout efficiency of the NV’s ground state spin.

arxiv-2203-02681.title: Electronic structure of higher-order Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates
arxiv-2203-02681.creator: Myung-Chul Jung, Jesse Kapeghian, Chase Hanson, Betül Pamuk, Antia S. Botana
arxiv-2203-02681.description: Abstract We analyze the electronic structure of the recently synthesized higher-order nickelate Ruddlesden-Popper phases La n+1 Ni n O 3n+1 ( n = 4 − 6 n=4-6 ) using first-principles calculations. For all materials, our results show large holelike Fermi surfaces with d x 2 − y 2 d_{x^{2}-y^{2}} character that closely resemble those of optimally hole-doped cuprates.

arxiv-2205-10510.title: Four sub-Jovian-mass planets detected by high-cadence microlensing surveys
arxiv-2205-10510.creator: Cheongho Han, Doeon Kim, Andrew Gould, Andrzej Udalski, Ian A. Bond, Valerio Bozza, Youn Kil Jung (Leading authors) Michael D. Albrow, Sun-Ju Chung, Kyu-Ha Hwang, Yoon-Hyun Ryu, In-Gu Shin, Yossi Shvartzvald, Jennifer C. Yee, Weicheng Zang, Sang-Mok Cha, Dong-Jin Kim, Seung-Lee Kim, Chung-Uk Lee, Do
arxiv-2205-10510.description: Abstract Aims. With the aim of finding short-term planetary signals, we investigated the data collected from the high-cadence microlensing surveys. Methods. From this investigation, we found four planetary systems with low planet-to-host mass ratios, including OGLE-2017-BLG-1691L, KMT-2021-BLG-0320L, KMT-2021-BLG-1303L, and KMT-2021-BLG-1554L.

arxiv-2205-13018.title: On the Reliability of Computing-in-Memory Accelerators for Deep Neural Networks
arxiv-2205-13018.creator: Zheyu Yan, Xiaobo Sharon Hu, and Yiyu Shi
arxiv-2205-13018.description: Abstract Computing-in-memory with emerging non-volatile memory (nvCiM) is shown to be a promising candidate for accelerating deep neural networks (DNNs) with high energy efficiency. However, most non-volatile memory (NVM) devices suffer from reliability issues, resulting in a difference between actual data involved in the nvCiM computation and the weight value trained in the data center.

arxiv-2309-12979.title: EgoCor: an R package to facilitate the use of exponential semi-variograms for modelling the local spatial correlation structure in social epidemiology
arxiv-2309-12979.creator: Julia Dyck, Jan-Ole Koslik, Odile Sauzet
arxiv-2309-12979.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Julia Dyck, Jan-Ole Koslik, Odile Sauzet. As an alternative to using administrative areas for the evaluation of small-area health inequalities, Sauzet et al. suggested to take an ego-centred approach and model the spatial correlation structure of health outcomes at the individual level. Existing tools for the analysis of spatial data in R might appear too complex to non-specialists which could limit the use of the approach.

arxiv-2411-05005.title: Diff-2-in-1: Bridging Generation and Dense Perception with Diffusion Models
arxiv-2411-05005.creator: Shuhong Zheng Zhipeng Bao Ruoyu Zhao Martial Hebert Yu-Xiong Wang
arxiv-2411-05005.description: Abstract Beyond high-fidelity image synthesis, diffusion models have recently exhibited promising results in dense visual perception tasks. However, most existing work treats diffusion models as a standalone component for perception tasks, employing them solely for off-the-shelf data augmentation or as mere feature extractors.

arxiv-2602-23959.title: Thinking with Images as Continuous Actions: Numerical Visual Chain-of-Thought
arxiv-2602-23959.creator: Kesen Zhao, Beier Zhu, Junbao Zhou, Xingyu Zhu, Zhongqi Yue, Hanwang Zhang
arxiv-2602-23959.description: Abstract Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) increasingly rely on visual chain-of-thought to perform region-grounded reasoning over images. However, existing approaches ground regions via either textified coordinates—causing modality mismatch and semantic fragmentation—or fixed-granularity patches that both limit precise region selection and often require non-trivial architectural changes.

pmc-11415249.title: Soil-Transmitted Helminths in Kindergarten Children: Prevalence, Intensity and Associated Factors in Bule Hora Town
pmc-11415249.creator: Wako Dedecha, Tibeso Gemechu, Oliyad Husen, Habtemu Jarso, Lenco Bati
pmc-11415249.description: Background: Soil-transmitted helminth (STH) infections are a common problem in Ethiopia. This parasite affects the physical and mental development of children, causing malnutrition and iron deficiency anaemia. However, there are inadequate studies that demonstrate the extent of STHs and associated factors among kindergarten children in South Ethiopia, particularly in the study area.

pmc-11451234.title: Leverage machine learning to identify key measures in hospital operations management: a retrospective study to explore feasibility and performance of four common algorithms
pmc-11451234.creator: Wantao Zhang, Yan Zhu, Liqun Tong, Guo Wei, Huajun Zhang
pmc-11451234.description: BackgroundMeasures in operations management are pivotal for monitoring and assessing various aspects of hospital performance. Existing literature highlights the importance of regularly updating key management measures to reflect changing trends and organizational goals. Advancements in machine learning (ML) have presented promising opportunities for enhancing the process of updating operations management measures. However, their specific application and performance remain relatively unexplored.

pmc-11532779.title: Radiotherapy and increased risk of second primary cancers in breast cancer survivors: An epidemiological and large cohort study
pmc-11532779.creator: Niuniu Hou, Zhe Wang, Yuwei Ling, Guangdong Hou, Bo Zhang, Xue Zhang, Mei Shi, Zhuling Chu, Yaoling Wang, Jun Hu, Chong Chen, Rui Ling
pmc-11532779.description: BackgroundRadiotherapy (RT) for breast cancer (BC) may raise the risk of second primary cancers (SPCs), a relationship inadequately studied.MethodsWe analyzed 248268 female BC patients from 9 SEER registries, 1988–2018, identifying SPCs >5 years after initial treatment, comparing SPC risks between RT and non-RT cohorts using Fine-Gray and Poisson regressions.ResultsOf all participants, 55.4 % received surgery and RT.

pmc-11541188.title: Author Correction: Global climate-change trends detected in indicators of ocean ecology
pmc-11541188.creator: B B Cael, Kelsey Bisson, Emmanuel Boss, Stephanie Dutkiewicz, Stephanie Henson
pmc-11541188.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ocean wavebands of MODIS-Aqua remote sensing reflectance were accidentally excluded. The correct version of the code is available at 10.5281/zenodo.13736237 and https://github.com/bbcael/Rrs_trends, as is the original version of the code which it replaces. After correcting these errors, the fraction of the ocean for which an ocean colour trend is detected is now 40% (previously 56%) at the 95% confidence level; a trend is now detected for 56% of the ocean at the 90% confidence level.

pmc-12389211.title: Nanotechnology-Enhanced Sunscreens: Balancing Efficacy, Safety, and Environmental Impact
pmc-12389211.creator: Ruchi Khobragade, Anis Ahmad Chaudhary, Mohamed A M Ali, Mayur Kale, Neha Raut, Pratik Ghive, Hassan A Rudayni, Krutika Nagpurkar, Milind Umekar, Rashmi Trivedi, Avi Domb, Jingyuan Wen
pmc-12389211.description: Sunscreen protects skin from harmful Ultra Violet (UV) rays, preventing skin diseases like cancer and premature aging. This review explores the role of nanotechnology in enhancing sunscreen formulations by incorporating green and sustainable ingredients. Nanoparticles such as titanium dioxide and zinc oxide effectively reflect UV rays, improving protection while minimizing white residue, thereby enhancing aesthetics, stability, and efficacy.

pmc-12585820.title: Psychosocial factors and susceptibility to upper respiratory infections in community‐dwelling older adults of Japan
pmc-12585820.creator: Noriko Okamoto, Hiroki Matsui, Hirohito Tsuboi
pmc-12585820.description: BackgroundUpper respiratory infections (URIs), including the common cold, can lead to community‐acquired pneumonia and pose significant risks for older adults. In this study, we aimed to examine the influence of psychosocial factors on URIs among community‐dwelling older adults.MethodsA cross‐sectional survey was administered to 500 community‐dwelling older adults via an internet research panel (386 males and 114 females).

pmc-12592482.title: Methylene blue as a redox additive in electrolytes for advanced charcoal-based hybrid supercapacitors
pmc-12592482.creator: Van Nhat Nguyen, An-Giang Nguyen, Thi Viet Bac Phung, Phi Long Nguyen
pmc-12592482.description: Carbon-based supercapacitor electrodes derived from biomass have recently garnered significant attention due to their low cost, natural abundance, and environmental sustainability. In this study, charcoal was pretreated using a simple ultrasonic method and was employed as the active electrode material in both three-electrode and symmetric supercapacitor configurations.

pmc-13219858.title: Outcomes Following Usage of All Suture Anchors for Rotator Cuff Repair
pmc-13219858.creator: Andrew Zhang, Joel Koshy, Neel Patel, Luke Tjoumakaris, Ari Clements, Henson Destine, Bradford Tucker, Fotios Tjoumakaris
pmc-13219858.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objectives:All-suture anchors are a recent addition that serve as an alternative to conventional suture anchors utilized for arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (RCR). All-suture anchors provide several benefits compared to conventional suture anchors. All-suture anchors have smaller insertion widths and require less bone removal for insertion, thus maintaining bone stability and allowing for more anchors to be used in a region where bone availability is compromised.

pmc-13451881.title: Skeletal Effects After Miniscrew-Assisted Rapid Palatal Expansion on Sagittal and Vertical Dimensions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13451881.creator: Bintao Xie, Lingling Zhang, Yanqin Lu
pmc-13451881.description: ObjectiveThis study evaluated the skeletal impact of miniscrew-assisted rapid palatal expansion (MARPE) in sagittal and vertical planes. We aimed to clarify how this treatment affects the jaw structure of late adolescent and adult patients.MethodsWe searched electronic databases for relevant literature. Study selection, quality appraisal, and data retrieval were completed by two authors independently.

pmc-13486580.title: A tonsil organoid model reveals Epstein–Barr virus–infected germinal center B cell states during primary infection
pmc-13486580.creator: Mahina Tabassum Mitul, Yizhe Sun, Timothy B. Yates, Suhas Sureshchandra, Jenna M. Kastenschmidt, Andrew M. Sorn, Zachary W. Wagoner, Erika M. Joloya, Arjun K. Nair, Allyssa Daugherty, Naresha Saligrama, Gurpreet Ahuja, Qiu Zhong, Douglas Trask, Carmy Forney, Rui Guo, Matthew T. Weirauch, Leah C. Kot
pmc-13486580.description: SignificanceEpstein–Barr virus (EBV) is a gamma-herpesvirus that persistently infects nearly all humans and is rarely associated with autoimmunity and cancer. The virus usually infects tonsillar B cells and persists long-term in memory B cells, but the process by which this transition happens remains unclear.
